newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps ease back bar steady naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps ease back bar steady naphtha.

text.p: European oil swaps eased back on Tuesday as crude slipped after the long holiday weekend in the U.K and U.S., traders said.
Refining margins also continued to be pressured. Shell cut runs by about 14 percent at Pernis, Rotterdam on Monday to echo similar cuts at Texaco and BP's Nerefco complex last week.
Brent crude CFDs, which were strongly boosted on Friday by a physical deal, eased back today.
Friday's buyer at July +17 cents picked up another Dated cargo on Tuesday at July +9 cents in a move that many in the market saw as an attempt to support what was thought to be a long CFD position.
The spread between this week and next week remained steady at about 23 cents.
May 27-30 was pegged around July Brent +5-6 cents compared with +7-8 cents on Friday while further out levels also weakened.
June 2-6 was down to July -18 cents from -16 cents and June 9-13 hovered around -19 cents against -13 cents.
High sulphur fuel oil swaps were pulled sharply lower on the back of heavy wet selling.
June barges dipped over $2 a tonne to $80-81 with July also losing $2-2.50 to $82-83. Phyiscal barges were heard done at $78 fob ARA with $77 fob rumoured, but not confirmed.
Dealers said one seller was particuarly keen to shift material in order to free up space for Russian fuel.
Low sulphur swaps were static showing little change from Friday.
Gasoline swaps slipped by $2 or so as the impetus to stock up on material ahead of an expected June 10 U.K budget evaporated with talk that the budget may be delayed.
Naphtha was steady on June and about 50 cents easier on July.
